text:
Aisha S: Customer reports duplicate external side-effect and double billing after our function-call API returned 202 then retried. They say the external action (send-invoice) fired twice. :alert:
Samir G: ok can you paste the request_id and the raw request body they sent?
Aisha S: req=req-9f8a2b4c, customer supplied this payload:```{
  "model": "redwood-legacy-001",
  "input": "Generate invoice and call send-invoice tool",
  "function_call": {
    "name": "send-invoice",
    "arguments": {
      "order_id": "ORD-44321",
      "amount": 124.50
    }
  }
}```
Aisha S: note: no idempotency token or client-provided invocation_id. They said they got HTTP 202 then retried after 8s and saw another successful execution.
Maya D: do we log tool-call execution ids server-side? we should be able to see if we invoked tool twice or if the external webhook retried.
jason.ops: pulled logs for req-9f8a2b4c, looks like two tool invocations from runtime with distinct internal run ids, timestamps 1719801234 and 1719801242. snippet:
```
[2024-10-18T15:20:34Z] req=req-9f8a2b4c run_id=run-a1 trigger=fncall send-invoice -> outgoing POST to https://payments.acme/api/invoice 200 OK
[2024-10-18T15:20:42Z] req=req-9f8a2b4c run_id=run-a2 trigger=fncall send-invoice -> outgoing POST to https://payments.acme/api/invoice 200 OK
```
Samir G: hm runtime retried the function-call path. Why would it retry after a 200 from the tool? any upstream 202s?
jason.ops: the runtime received 202 from our internal tool-proxy for the first send, because the proxy enqueued job and returned 202. runtime policy treats 202 as non-terminal for fncalls and will attempt backoff-retries up to 3 unless tool reports an execution-id. we ended up triggering the proxy again on the next attempt.
Maya D: so double-exec chain: client missing idempotency -> runtime sees 202 -> runtime retries -> proxy enqueues duplicate job -> external system processes both -> customer gets two invoices and two charges.
Aisha S: customer is asking for immediate remediation and refund. also want steps to prevent. :eyes:
Samir G: short-term: we can manually flag req-9f8a2b4c as duplicate and coordinate refund with customer. long-term: 2 changes: (1) require/propagate client-provided idempotency keys for fncalls (invocation_id) and (2) change retry semantics so 202 from tool-proxy returns a stable execution_id we persist and never re-invoke.
Maya D: agree. also want to update docs and SDKs to recommend client idempotency header `X-Redwood-Invocation-Id` and example pattern.
jason.ops: created a mitigation runbook entry in #incidents, also added a temporary check to not retry if the tool-proxy returns header `Redwood-Execution-Id`. but we need a PR to persist that id across retries.
oncall-bot: NOTE: Incident created INC-2024-0917 by jason.ops (severity P2)
Samir G: repro steps for eng:
1) Client sends fncall with no invocation_id, runtime forwards to proxy.
2) Proxy returns 202 Accepted with no execution id (simulating async enqueue).
3) Runtime treats 202 as transient and retries after backoff => duplicate invocation.
4) External processes both and returns 200 twice.
Example client request to reproduce quickly:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxxx' \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-legacy-001","function_call":{"name":"send-invoice","arguments":{"order_id":"ORD-44321","amount":124.50}}}'
```
Samir G: suggested quick fix PR: treat 202 from tool-proxy as terminal only if proxy returns `Redwood-Execution-Id` header; otherwise return a 502 to client so client retries instead of runtime. But sending 502 is risky. alternative: persist an optimistic lock when forwarding first attempt for a request id scoped to (customer, function_name, arguments hash) to dedupe within 30s.
Maya D: SDK change: auto-generate `X-Redwood-Invocation-Id` if not set and send it with fncall requests. Serverside we should prefer client id over our optimistic lock TTL.
Aisha S: customer wants timeline. can we have a short-term rollback/patch and a rollout plan?
jason.ops: I'll own the emergency patch to read and persist `Redwood-Execution-Id` header and skip retries if present. can roll to staging in 2 hours and prod in 6-8 hours if tests pass.
Samir G: I'll draft the spec for idempotency key + dedupe UX and PR for SDKs. Maya please add docs and a sample snippet.
Aisha S: thanks all. I'll update the customer with the incident ref INC-2024-0917 and ETA for patch.
Maya D: also adding a note to billing to absorb this one while we patch (to avoid churn).
Aisha S: closing loop here, next updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
